The picker's rules and numbers, the first forty knocks with three answers each and every echo, Hear someone out with its five mood wrappers, and the Wall. Text is never in the save, only ids. Numbers are starting values; none are playtested. A knock whose needs wait on a later slice is 'disabled' and says which.

flags.shown: {name} will remember that.
flags.readBy: The courtroom (Part 23): the question the prosecution asks four times

flags.shown: {name} will remember you asked.
flags.readBy: The Hand-Off (Part 23), if they're the heir

flags.shown: It's what the team says at a door now.
The region's first headline will be a guess.
The ferry's free for {name} this region.
Every Ledger line has a name from now on.
The Ledger shows amounts. {name} keeps the names in a second book.
A waiver will be offered.
{name} will take the Garage when it's needed.
{name} will say it again, if it comes to it.
{name} will tell the next new Grunt the story.
The Card now knows: {name}, not a house call.
{name} won't freeze again.
{name} will notice first if the Creed and the Ledger stop matching.
{name}'s doubts will come a job sooner.
A dated slip in the mole file.
{name}'s quest has its first thread.
{name}'s mum will come to the café.
A letter's pinned by {name}'s bunk: “As long as you're eating.”
The Roster shows birthdays from now on.
Dispatch will show squad names.
The squad's name will be heard at their door.
The Hero's File has the squad's name anyway.
{name} has the map table.
{name} will ask again at seventeen.
flags.readBy: Nobody yet: the run's not that long

flags.shown: {name} has a friend on the Roster now.
The man at the door's been named to them.
The detective's notebook has a blank line.
The detective's list is a day behind.
Tomorrow's Board has “Walk into the station” on it.
It's in the diary, under “things we're not going to”.
A handshake. Their plate stays on the bunk.
{name} unpacked.
It's a custom now, on the Board in small letters.
The Common Room has a ballot tin.
The cat's called Ledger.
flags.readBy: The Office, every scene from now

flags.shown: A small figure, running. Nothing else.
flags.readBy: Nobody. The game doesn't say who

flags.shown: {name} will keep that one, whatever else.
They can't be dismissed by an Executive alone.
Their Oath will be a line shorter.
{name} has a reason now.
The Potion's on {name}'s shelf.
The File's first page gains a line.
The Pen's cards gain a line in {name}'s hand.
The Pen can send one home.
The Pen's first card says Biscuit.
The owner finds it on the step at dawn.
The Patron will stop one job, once.
The Patron will ask again, about something worse.
The Mess has a second.
Where the Boss eats is counted from tonight.
{name} will ask next time.
{name}'s off the money.
The bottle's in the Office drawer.
The Ledger was covered, and nothing was said.
{name} will fill in Not known on Cards.
Heat's arrow will show it tomorrow, if it lands.
One name on the list is the detective's.
The constable will come with the warning.
They're a standing pair from now on.
The word Kind moves on {name}'s card, to the talent's side.
A Work will be offered: the cannery, paid.
Her next letter has a line in it.
The Hero will arrive knowing one room.
The next Take's Card will say it.
Otis moves the Vault's key that night.
The long way back from Corruption starts.
They've seen the window.
A mark, the gentlest in the mode.
They remember the cat.
The neighbour's noted which.
It sleeps in the Office from now on.

flags.shown: They're back, at their old rank.

wall.what: A mug, washed, on the desk
A bottle, in the desk drawer
A coat on the peg by the door. Nobody takes it
A birthday card, signed by everyone
The uniform, in crayon. The colours are right
A drawing: the Boss, in a very large hat
A summons. A date, a room and a name
The Ledger's first page, every name on it

text.doorDone: The door's shut. The corridor's quiet.
text.cantShut: This one can't be shut out.
text.acted: The night's one action is used.
text.hearShut: “Nothing. I'm fine. Was there something you wanted?”
text.hearPlain: Nothing much. It was a day. I did it.
text.hearAsked: About what you asked me. In the yard. I've not stopped turning it over.
text.takeDownGap: The gap stays: a paler rectangle.
text.wallEmpty: Nothing's up yet. It's still a wall.
text.hushed: {name} won't knock again this region. They're choosing it.
text.logKnock: Night. {who} at the door: “{says}” The Boss: “{answer}”
text.logShut: Night. {who} at the door. Not tonight.

warmExtra.voice: And I've started saying “we” about this place. I heard myself.
warmExtra.hands: And I've stopped checking where the exits are when I come in. I only noticed tonight.
warmExtra.eyes: And I watch your door last thing. To see it's shut. I don't know why I told you that.
warmExtra.nerve: And I'd stand on any door for you. That's not a thing I say.
warmExtra.books: And I've stopped keeping my own copy. Of anything. That's new.
warmExtra.wheels: And I keep the tank full now. In case you need to go somewhere. Anywhere.
warmExtra.heart: And you're eating badly. I've noticed. I'll say no more.

byTalent.voice: A woman on the corner asked what we're for. I told her. She listened all the way through.
byTalent.hands: There's a latch on the yard gate that sticks on the third try. I've fixed it twice. It likes being stuck.
byTalent.eyes: The baker's started leaving the side door open after six. I don't think it's for us.
byTalent.nerve: Nobody tried the door today. I stood on it anyway. You never know which day it is.
byTalent.books: The figures came out round today. They never come out round. I checked them twice.
byTalent.wheels: There's a short cut past the canal if you don't mind the bins. I don't mind the bins.
byTalent.heart: Somebody's Pokémon came in limping and went out running. That's the whole day, for me.

byPerson.otis: Door's sticking again. I like a door that sticks. You hear it.
byPerson.faye: There's a lock on the chemist's that's older than the building. Somebody moved it there. I'd like to know from where.
byPerson.tobi: I learned a word. “Fiduciary.” Ngozi said it. I've been saying it all day. Nobody's told me what it means.
byPerson.lux: The woman at number nine waters her plants at four in the morning. I don't think she sleeps either.
byPerson.ngozi: The books balance. I'd like you to know how rarely that's true of anything.
byPerson.tomasz: Second gear's going. I can feel it in my foot. She's got another month.
byPerson.hortense: They've stopped leaving the crusts. That's a happy kitchen. You can tell a place by its crusts.
byPerson.vikram: I counted the till four times today and it was right four times. I didn't know what to do with myself.
byPerson.sioned: I rewrote the notice. Then I put it back how it was. It was better. I don't like that it was better.
byPerson.kwabena: There's a lad on the neighbour's door who stands well. Feet right. I nodded at him. He nodded back. That's all.
byPerson.beatriz: There's a street on the map that isn't there. I walked it. It's a wall. Somebody drew a street on purpose.
byPerson.obadiah: Thirty years ago a pound of sugar was eleven. I only mention it.
byPerson.chidi: The swallows have gone. Three days early. I've written it down. I don't know what I've written it down for.
byPerson.rahel: I said the pitch today and a man said, “You don't believe that.” I did, though. I checked.
byPerson.junseo: There's a back road past the mill. Nobody uses it. I don't either. I just like knowing.
byPerson.halima: Nobody came in today. Not one. I cleaned the whole room twice. That's a good day and I hated it.
byPerson.arlo: Somebody in the Game Corner hit three sevens today. I could hear it from the street. The house doesn't mind. It never minds.
byPerson.mirela: The new cleaner at the Silph tower mops the lifts last. Wrong way round. I nearly went in to tell her.
byPerson.dov: Saw a lad on a bike on Cycling Road with no hands on the bars. Showing off. I used to do that. I waved.
byPerson.nanami: There's a Gastly at the Tower that comes to the window when I walk past. It's not unhappy. It just likes the window.
byPerson.garrick: The Anne's due Thursday. I always know when she's due. I can feel the harbour lean.
byPerson.pilar: I did a practice paper on the bus. Got the type chart one right. First time. I didn't tell anyone till now.
byPerson.efua: A woman asked me to look at her lock today. Not to open it. Just to tell her if it was any good. It wasn't.
byPerson.walther: A child asked me how to spell “Celadon”. I told her. She thanked me like I'd given her something.
byPerson.sooah: Somebody's left a scooter by the canal. Not stolen. Just left. I keep checking it's still there.
byPerson.ignatius: Someone called me by my name in the shop today. My actual name. I put the bread down and went back for it.
byPerson.catriona: The warden ate soup today. Proper soup, with the lumps in. That's teeth. That's nearly teeth.
byPerson.yevgeny: The lights flickered on Route 10 tonight. It's not the Plant. It's not anything. I went and looked anyway.
byPerson.hinata: The switchboard's still in my head. Seventy lines. I hear one ringing when it's quiet. Nobody picks it up.
byPerson.barnaby: Smelled charcoal in the yard tonight. Somebody's burning it wrong. Too green. I nearly went and showed them.
byPerson.tsering: I did the first turn of the piece in the corridor. Just the first turn. Don't tell anyone.
byPerson.eamon: There's a lamp on the harbour wall that flickers at nine. Every night. I keep meaning to see to it.
byPerson.sachiko: Fifty years over that cellar and the first thing I did here was look for the stairs down. Habit.
byPerson.cosmin: Pressure in my ears today and I wasn't anywhere near the water. Weather's turning, or I am.
byPerson.adaeze: Somebody's Pokémon has a cough in the next street. Dry, at night. I've written down what it needs. I'll leave it on the step.
byPerson.ruairi: Scyther moulted. You keep the old blade or you don't. I kept it. I always keep it.
byPerson.mwajuma: Walked past an empty stall today and priced it in my head. Rent, rates, the lot. Can't help it.
byPerson.leif: Rang a bell in my sleep again. My arms ache in the morning like I did. Funny, that.
byPerson.quyen: There's a pattern on the Board's wood grain. It isn't anything. I've been looking at it for an hour.
byPerson.dermot: Counted the stops between here and the station. Eleven. I'd have done it in nine.
byPerson.keala: Wind's from the south. Good sailing tomorrow, if anyone was sailing. Nobody is.
byPerson.rohan: I added up the week in my head on the stairs. It balances. I don't trust it when it balances.
byPerson.imelda: Somebody left a flower on the sill. Wrong season for it. I'd like to know where they got it.
byPerson.tavita: Sat still for a whole hour today. On purpose. Brawly would laugh. I'm telling you so somebody knows.
byPerson.greta: Barometer's dropping and the sky says it isn't. One of them's lying. It's usually not the barometer.
byPerson.babajide: I tied the knots on the washing line again. Somebody'd done them like a landlubber. No offence.
byPerson.miyu: I wrote my brother a letter. I'm not sending it. I just wanted it written down somewhere.
byPerson.orsolya: There's ash on the windowsill. Fine, grey, the good kind. I could make a flute out of this street.
byPerson.declan: I put a trick on the back door. Nothing nasty. You'll know it when you find it.
byPerson.lakshmi: Marked somebody's spelling today. They didn't ask. I couldn't stop myself. Old habits.
byPerson.finlay: Held my breath in the bath. Three minutes. I'm out of practice.
byPerson.zainab: I still check the key's in my pocket before I sleep. Every night. It's always there.
byPerson.sp-teller: Counted the takings twice. Out of habit. It's right. I'm sorry I checked.
byPerson.sp-uncle: My uncle's still telling everyone. I've stopped correcting him. It's better than what's true.
byPerson.sp-always: I've always wanted to. I keep saying it. It's still true.
byPerson.sp-meowth: Saw a Meowth on the wall eating out of somebody's hand. Nobody does that either.
byPerson.sp-junior: She'll ask me how you are. I've not decided what I'll say.
byPerson.sp-other: I nearly said 'ours' about the other lot today. Caught it. Took a minute.
byPerson.sp-gran: Gran sent a cake. It's in the Common Room. Don't let Otis near it.
byPerson.sp-scared: Walked past the Center and nobody looked at me. Nobody looked at me at all. That was new.
byPerson.sp-cheap: Found a ten on the stairs. Put it in the jar. Cheap isn't the same as a thief.
byPerson.sp-builder: The window frame's out by a hair. I built it. I can see it from the bed.
byPerson.sp-road: The kid's Pokémon was fine in the end. I checked. I always check.
byPerson.sp-constable: Old boots by the door. Constable's boots. I'll give them away when I've decided I'm not one.
byPerson.sp-nobody: Everyone was here at supper. Every single one. I counted.

knocks.title: The first hire
knocks.says: (In the doorway of a room with one chair in it.) “Who was here before you?”

answers.say: I don't know. Somebody who left in a hurry.
answers.reply: Right. …There's a mug in the sink. I'll wash it.
It's got somebody's height marks on the kitchen door. (A pause.) But all right.
It will to whoever comes after us.

knocks.title: The ferry woman
knocks.says: “The ferry woman asked who we are. I didn't know what to tell her.”

answers.reply: …That'll do. I'll tell her that.
She'll make something up, then. They do.

answers.say: What did you want to tell her?
answers.reply: That I'd not had a job in two years and now I've a coat with a letter on it.

knocks.title: A line on the Ledger
knocks.says: “There's a line on the Ledger I'd like you to look at before I total it.” (A name, written where the amount goes.)

answers.reply: I'd intended to. I wanted to see if you'd make me take it out.
It's ₽400. It's also a Mrs. Okafor. I'll put the one you asked for.
A widow with a fish stall. She paid in coins. I counted them twice out of respect.

knocks.title: The Pen
knocks.says: “I've been treating what's in the Pen. I wasn't asked. Is that all right?”

answers.say: Yes. Put it on the Infirmary's list.
answers.reply: Then I'll want the latch left off between nine and ten. I can't do it through bars.
They're patients. I'll do it in my own time and you needn't know.
I know all eight. I've been reading the collars.

knocks.title: The float
knocks.says: “I could've driven off. Tonight. I had the float in the van. I'm telling you because I didn't.”

answers.say: I know you could. That's why you had it.
answers.reply: …Oh. (Very pleased, and trying not to be.)
Where'd I go? …No. That's not it. I'd have had to stop being here.

answers.say: Don't tell me things like that.
answers.reply: Right. Sorry. I thought you'd want to—right.

knocks.title: “I froze”
knocks.says: “I froze. On the door. You'll have seen. It's not on my card. I just did.”

answers.reply: Did you? (They wait. They nod, either way.)

answers.say: What was on the other side of the door?
answers.reply: A man my dad's age. In his slippers.
No.

knocks.title: “I'd like to know it was true”
knocks.says: “I talked someone into it today. I'm good at it. I'd like to know it was true, what I said.”

answers.reply: Good. Then I'll say it again tomorrow, and I'll not have to look at the floor.
“Enough.” That's a word I use on other people.
(They tell you. Your team's own pitch, once, from the outside.) “{creedLine}”

knocks.title: The wage that isn't spent
knocks.says: “Somebody on the Roster's not spending their wage.”

answers.reply: (A name.) I've not said why. I don't know why. I only see what's there.
It is. I'll stop looking at it.
…Batteries. And my brother.

knocks.title: The collar
knocks.says: “I took it. It was easy. It had a name on the collar.” (They're holding the collar, not the Pokémon.)

answers.say: Write the name on the card.
answers.reply: I already have. “Biscuit.” I wanted you to have to read it.
Tonight? (“Tonight.”) …I'll get my coat.
I'll not take another, then. That's me telling you, not asking.

knocks.title: “Would he have done that?”
knocks.says: (After the day's worst job.) “Would he have done that? My old one. I'm asking.”

answers.reply: No. He'd not have let me ask.
I didn't. That's rather the point of me.
Then I've learned nothing in fourteen years. Good night.

knocks.title: “My mum's asked what I do”
knocks.says: “My mum's asked what I do.”

answers.say: Tell her the Front. You work at the café.
answers.reply: I can't cook. (“You carry things.”) I can do that.
She'll cry. (“Will she tell anyone?”) No. She'll just cry.

answers.say: What d'you want to tell her?
answers.reply: That I've got mates.

knocks.title: A birthday
knocks.says: “It's my birthday. Nobody knows. I don't know why I'm telling you.”

answers.reply: …Thanks. That's all. I'll go.
They'll make a thing of it. (“Yes.”)
{age}. (It's on their card. You could've looked.)

knocks.title: The squad's name
knocks.says: “My squad's got a name. I didn't give it to them. They did.” (The Late Shift.)

answers.reply: They'll be insufferable.
The Late Shift. (Embarrassed.)
This one does. I only came to tell you.

knocks.title: “You've made me a department”
knocks.says: “The room's too big for me. I'm a cook. You've made me a department.”

answers.reply: Under me. Listen to you. …The quiet one. She peels properly.

answers.say: It's the same job. More pans.
answers.reply: It's forty covers. I did forty covers at the ward. I'd hoped I was done.
No. I want you to come and eat in it.

knocks.title: “What'd you want kept?”
knocks.says: “If you weren't here tomorrow. What'd you want kept?”

answers.say: A rule. (One of the team's lines.)
answers.reply: I'll keep that one. Whatever else.
Them? …All right. Them.
Then I'll not get attached.

knocks.title: A Grunt who met the Hero
knocks.says: “The kid asked me why I'm in it. I didn't have one. I've been thinking.”

answers.reply: (Their reason, now they've one.)
That's what I said. The kid said, “Is that all?”
(You tell them: “{creedLine}”) …That's better than mine.

knocks.title: A Grunt who lost to the Hero
knocks.says: “They gave me a Potion. After. Who does that?”

answers.reply: I was going to. I've not used it. It's on my shelf.
…It was given to me.

answers.say: Somebody who's going to be trouble.
answers.reply: No. Somebody who's going to be all right. That's different.

knocks.title: Skims
knocks.says: “Before you count it. It's two hundred short. It's my sister's rent. I'll put it back.”

answers.reply: I didn't think asking was a thing here.
Friday. Yes.
That's fair.

knocks.title: Drinks
knocks.says: “I missed the morning. I'm not going to say sorry again. I'm going to ask if you'd take the bottle.”

answers.reply: (They do.) There's another in the cistern. I'm telling you so I've told someone.
I know it is. I thought I'd try the easy way first.
The Ledger. Thirty years I've never missed a ledger.

knocks.title: Doubts
knocks.says: “I stopped. On the stair. I'd like to know if I was wrong to.”

answers.say: No. Tell me what you saw.
answers.reply: (What stopped them: the job's Not known field, found out.)

answers.say: Yes. You cost us the job.
answers.reply: I did. I'd do it again, I think. That's the trouble.
…That's the first time anyone's said that to me in a uniform.

knocks.title: Talks
knocks.says: “I said something. In the pub. I don't know who heard.”

answers.reply: (They say. It's a real fact of the run.)
(They list them. One's a name from the detective's list.)
It's where my mates are.

knocks.title: Loves someone on the other side
knocks.says: “She's a constable. I've not told her. I've not told you. Now I've told you.”

answers.reply: That's it? I'd a bag packed.
No. And she won't. From either of us.
…Don't.

knocks.title: Proud
knocks.says: “I'm not taking orders from a boy of nineteen.”

answers.say: Then tell him how it's done, and let him give the order.
answers.reply: …That's taking orders with extra steps. (Through the door:) Right. You. Listen.
I am. I wanted it said that I mind.
(In the doorway: “I didn't ask for it.”) You can't give it me. So do it properly.

knocks.title: Kind
knocks.says: “I gave it back. The strongbox. I'm on the card as a flaw. Am I?”

answers.reply: Then would you have it taken off?
I thought so. I just wanted it from you.
Wages. A cannery's. Friday's.

knocks.title: “I'm eighteen”
knocks.says: “I'm eighteen.” (They aren't. They're asking to go on a job the minors' lock won't let them near.)

answers.reply: …Who told you? (“You did. In your own writing.”)

answers.say: Then show me something with your age on it.
answers.reply: (They can't. They stand there.)
Because the others go. And they're rubbish.

knocks.title: A local, in person
knocks.says: (Having walked past the door Grunt.) “You've a man at my door every Friday. I've come to see whose he is.”

answers.reply: (They don't sit.) I wanted to see if you'd say so.
Polite. That's what's so awful.
He's got your letter on his coat.

knocks.title: The detective
knocks.says: “I'm not here officially. I've a question. It's not in the notebook. Why the bakery? I can't make it fit.”

answers.reply: …Hm. (They don't write it down. That's the point.)
No. I'd not either.

answers.say: Come in. You'll have had no tea.
answers.reply: (They come in. They have the tea. They see the Common Room and nothing else.)

knocks.title: A canon Boss's messenger

who.outside: A messenger, with a fruit basket

knocks.says: (A fruit basket. A card: “Regards.”)

answers.reply: (It's kept.)
(It goes back.)
(One goes.)

knocks.title: The Hero's mother
knocks.says: “I'm told you run this. I'm not here to shout. My child's walking toward you. I'd like to know what they'll find.”

answers.reply: I'll hold you to that. I've nothing to hold you with. I'll hold you anyway.
That's honest. I'd rather have had the other.
(She's walked round.)

knocks.title: A child from the School
knocks.says: (Brought by a Grunt who couldn't say no.) “Miss says you're the baddies. Are you?”

answers.reply: I'm sometimes.

answers.say: What does Miss say baddies do?
answers.reply: Take things and not say sorry.
Miss says baddies say that.

knocks.title: Somebody who's leaving
knocks.says: (In their own coat, with a bag.) “I'm going. I wanted to say it to you, not leave a note.”

answers.reply: …Right. Yes.
A wage on time. And to be asked, once. (They unpack.)
(They do. On the chair.)

knocks.title: Somebody who left, come back
knocks.says: “Is the bunk still—”

answers.reply: (They can't say anything for a moment.)
Course it has. I only— (From the corridor: “They can have it. I'll go on the floor.”)
It was quieter than I thought. Out there.

knocks.title: The mole
knocks.says: “Is the Vault always the second door past the kitchen, in these places?”

answers.reply: Thanks. I get lost.
(A reason. A good one, either way.)
I'd rather not ask the door.

knocks.title: The mole, found
knocks.says: (Part 11 section 8: the scene, with its four ways through. It takes the Night's knock.)

answers.reply: (Part 11.)
(Part 11.)
(Part 11.)

knocks.title: Whoever runs the Lab
knocks.says: “I didn't volunteer.”

answers.reply: Who'd you put on instead? (They wait for a name.)
Do they.
…Tonight? With them still in it?

knocks.title: A Pokémon
knocks.says: (It's not a knock. It's at the door. It wants to sleep in the Office.)

answers.reply: (It gets on the chair.)
(It goes, and looks round once.)
(It leans.)

knocks.title: Nobody, and a drawing
knocks.says: (The door. Nobody there. A drawing on the mat: the uniform, in crayon. The colours are right.)

answers.reply: (It goes up.)
(The door Grunt pins it up in the morning.)
(A small figure, running.)

knocks.title: Nobody, and a summons
knocks.says: (The door. Nobody. A summons on the mat.)

answers.reply: (The list's first three items, in legal words.)
“It's a date, a room and a name. I'll put it in the diary. Under ‘things we're not going to’.”
(It was served. Burning it's on the list now.)

knocks.title: A vote
knocks.says: (The rest behind them in the corridor.) “We took a vote. We've not done that before. We'd like to tell you what it was about.” (The name of the cat.)

answers.reply: Unanimous, less one. (The one's named, and is delighted to be.)

answers.say: You don't need my leave to vote.
answers.reply: We know. We wanted you to know we know.
You'd a vote. The kitchen cast it for you. They said you'd want the cat called Ledger.

knocks.title: The Hero
knocks.says: (Opening the wrong door.) “Sorry. I was looking for the— is this the way out?”

answers.reply: Thanks. …Nice window.

answers.say: Sit down a minute. Finish that.
answers.reply: (They do. They talk about the soup. None of it's about the team.)
Right. Sorry.
